correctness.rationale: For n=3m+1, each paired vertex-pair of L(K_n) covers exactly three K_n ground vertices and the domination requirement covers at least n-1. Equality forces disjoint centered triples and a unique unmatched ground vertex. Removing one selected K_n edge yields exactly two incident replacement edges that preserve the structure, per selected edge. The resulting connected position graph is a bouquet of m four-cycles whose edge transpositions generate S_(3m+1), proving connectivity. The 4m-degree, edge count and exhaustive two-family triangle census follow. Direct brute-force verification at n=4,7 and independent slot BFS through m=3 passed; the general proof is not inferred from them.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Two nearby encodings of the same configurations are not equivalent assertions about adjacency: the former changes both selected vertices in a backup pair and can jump over infeasible intermediate states, while the new move changes only one adjacent selected vertex at each step. A connected graph under the former moves need not be connected under the latter.

value.rationale: The stricter operational motion of one guard while retaining an optimal paired-backup configuration is distinct from replacing two guards as a whole induced-matching edge. The infinite-family connectedness theorem, exact vertex-transitive 4m-regular graph, edges and local triangle structure identify the precise feasible exchange topology in a natural tight-coverage family. The family is motivated by saturation of the 3-ground-vertices-per-pair bound; it is not an arbitrary finite slice. The covered optimum-state count is clearly treated as prerequisite rather than originality evidence.
